content:
**Key observations:**
- Stem split open lengthwise revealing the internal cavity
- Interior shows bleached/white-tan pith tissue — classic "timber" appearance
- Dark black hard bodies visible inside the stem cavity — these are **sclerotia**, the defining diagnostic structure of *Sclerotinia sclerotiorum*
- Outer stem is tan/brown and dead; surrounding foliage also desiccated
- No leaf spotting, no mycelium mat visible externally

The presence of sclerotia (hard, black, irregular bodies) inside a hollowed, bleached stem is the definitive hallmark of Sclerotinia stem rot (timber rot). No other class in this list produces sclerotia inside the stem cavity.
